blocks.text: I can explain how to use long multiplication to multiply two 2-digit numbers with regrouping.
We will use long multiplication to solve Olympic problems.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: Any of the multiplication results we get leading up to an overall multiplication result is a partial product.
The process of unitising and exchanging between place values is known as regrouping. For example, 10 ones can be regrouped for one ten; one ten can be regrouped for 10 ones.

blocks.text: Regrouping means exchanging between place values.
We regroup when numbers bridge 10 or 100.

slides.title: What is known? What is unknown?

blocks.text: Each of the 35 sections of a stadium has 48 seats. How many seats are there in total?

items.title: Known
items.sub: 35 sections, 48 seats in each. These are the factors.

items.title: Unknown
items.sub: The total number of seats. The product is missing.

blocks.text: Long multiplication. The larger number goes first, so 48 is at the top and 35 is underneath.

items: 48 × 5 ones. 5 × 8 ones = 40 ones. Write 0 in the ones column and regroup 40 ones for 4 tens. Record the 4 at the top.
5 × 4 tens = 20 tens. Add the 4 tens: 24 tens. That is 240.

blocks.label: First partial product
blocks.text: The first partial product is **240**.

items: Put 0 as the next placeholder, so every part we work out now is a multiple of 10.
3 tens × 8 ones = 24 tens. Write 4 in the tens column and regroup 2 hundreds.
3 tens × 4 tens = 12 hundreds. Add the 2 hundreds: 14 hundreds. That is 1,400.

blocks.text: Sum the partial products. There are 1,680 seats altogether.
There are 26 stands around a pool with 57 seats in each stand. This is 57 × 26.

items: 57 × 6: 6 × 7 ones = 42 ones. Write 2 in the ones column and regroup 40 ones for 4 tens.
6 × 5 tens = 30 tens. Add the 4 tens: 34 tens. The first partial product is 342.
Put 0 as a placeholder.
57 × 20: 2 tens × 7 ones = 14 tens (140). Write 4 in the tens column and regroup 1 hundred.
2 tens × 5 tens = 10 hundreds. Add the 1 hundred: 11 hundreds. The second partial product is 1,140.

blocks.label: How many times did we regroup?
blocks.text: Twice: once when we multiplied by 6 and again when we multiplied by 20.
In the Olympic village there are 63 buildings. Each building has 28 beds. How many beds are there in total?

blocks.q: Which multiplication finds the total number of beds?
blocks.why: 63 buildings is one factor and 28 beds is the other factor. The product is missing.

blocks.text: Sam used long multiplication and looked at the regrouping in his working.

blocks.label: Is Sam correct?
blocks.text: No. Sam regrouped incorrectly. The digits were reversed when they were recorded as exchanges. Write the regrouped values the right way round at the top.

blocks.q: Where do we record the regrouped values?
options: At the top, above the factors
We do not need to record them
blocks.why: They are included at the top of the layout as a reminder to add them on in the next calculation.

blocks.text: There are 56 teams with 33 members in each team. How many athletes altogether? This is 56 × 33, with the larger factor first.

items: 56 × 3: 6 × 3 ones = 18 ones. Regroup 10 ones for 1 ten.
5 tens × 3 = 15 tens. Add the 1 ten: 16 tens. The first partial product is 168.
Put a placeholder 0. 56 × 30: 3 tens × 6 ones = 18 tens (180). Write 8 in the tens column and regroup 1 hundred.
3 tens × 5 tens = 15 hundreds. Add the 1 hundred: 16 hundreds. The second partial product is 1,680.

blocks.text: There are 1,848 athletes altogether. Bingo!
When multiplying with long multiplication, you always begin with the ones.
Andeep got 1,656. There are two problem cards. Card one: 45 countries, each awarded 62 medals. Card two: 24 countries, each sending 69 athletes.

items: Card one has factors 45 and 62.
Card two has factors 24 and 69. 4 × 9 = 36, so the ones digit is 6.
1,656 has a ones digit of 6, so the answer belongs to card two.

blocks.label: Advice for Andeep
blocks.text: Look at the ones digits of the factors. Multiply them and check the ones digit of your answer.
Use the ones digits to check answers.

blocks.q: Which multiplication gives a product with a ones digit of 4?
blocks.why: 3 × 8 = 24, so the ones digit is 4. (5 × 6 = 30 and 0 × 2 = 0 give a ones digit of 0.)

blocks.q: Match each problem to the multiplication equation that solves it.
Use long multiplication to answer each question.

items: We can calculate the partial products and add the partial products to recombine when using long multiplication.
We can regroup when numbers bridge 10 or 100.

blocks.text: Record the regrouped values at the top and put the 0 placeholder before you multiply by the tens.

flashcards.back:
The process of unitising and exchanging between place values.

10 ones can be regrouped for one ten; one ten can be regrouped for 10 ones.

flashcards.front: When can we regroup in long multiplication?

flashcards.back: Any of the multiplication results we get leading up to an overall multiplication result.

flashcards.front: In a word problem, what are the factors and what is the product?
flashcards.back:
The factors are the two known numbers. The product is the unknown (missing) total.

35 sections × 48 seats: the total number of seats is the product.

flashcards.front: Why do we put a 0 placeholder before the second partial product?
flashcards.back: So all the bits we work out next are multiples of 10 (all multiples of 10 have a 0 in the ones column).

flashcards.front: 48 × 35: what are the two partial products and the product?
57 × 26: what are the two partial products and the product?
56 × 33: what are the two partial products and the product?
Where do we record regrouped values in these lessons?
flashcards.back: At the top, above the factors.

flashcards.front: Which digits do you multiply first in long multiplication?
flashcards.back: The ones. You always begin with the ones.

flashcards.front: How can the ones digits help you check an answer?
flashcards.back:
Multiply the ones digits of the factors. The ones digit of the product must match.

24 × 69: 4 × 9 = 36, so the ones digit is 6 (24 × 69 = 1,656).

flashcards.front: What went wrong when Sam’s regrouping was incorrect?
flashcards.back: The digits were reversed when they were recorded as exchanges.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Explain how to use long multiplication to multiply two 2-digit numbers with regrouping
worksheet.instructions: Use long multiplication with the larger factor at the top. Remember to regroup and to put in the 0 placeholder. Write each answer as a number (you do not need to write units).

questions.prompt: Task A: There are 76 torch handlers for each leg of the relay. There are 48 legs. How many torch handlers are involved in total?
Task A: Each of the 53 Olympic snack stands sells 67 snack boxes per day. How many snack boxes are sold each day across all the stands?
Task A: The Olympic village has 82 flag poles, and each flag pole needs 45 feet of rope. How many feet of rope are needed in total?
Task A: Each display case at the Olympic museum can hold 96 medals, and there are 34 display cases. How many medals can be displayed in total?
Task A: A replica Olympic torch costs £87. 59 torches are sold on Saturday. How many pounds is spent on replica torches?
Task B: In an Olympic athletics team, each team has 33 members. There are 56 teams. How many athletes are participating in total?
Task B: During the marathon, there are 36 water stations. Each station is stocked with 72 bottles of water. How many bottles of water are distributed in total?
Task B: Andeep got the answer 1,656. Which factors did his problem use: 45 and 62, or 24 and 69?
